### Review Cycle Time

> Figures here are SciRev self-reports (n = 10 reviews, https://scirev.org/reviews/studies-in-higher-education/ and journal page https://scirev.org/journal/studies-in-higher-education/, retrieved 2026-11-23) plus the editors' stated aim in the archived instructions. The publisher's journal-metrics block (about page, https://www.tandfonline.com/journals/cshe20/about-this-journal, read 2026-11-23) prints averages of 8 days from submission to first decision and 70 days from submission to first post-review decision; it says speed data are updated every six months from the prior six months.

| Stage | Typical Time | Notes |
|-------|-------------|-------|
| **Time to first decision** | Publisher page: 8 days average from submission to first decision, and 70 days average from submission to first post-review decision (see the note above this table). Immediate (desk) rejections in SciRev: 13, 19 and 168 days (3 reports; mean 66 days as printed on the journal page); the 168-day report says the editors could not find reviewers. The archived instructions (2022-12-20) say the editors aim to tell authors within 10 working days of a desk rejection or of a decision to send the paper out | n = 3 immediate rejections; self-reported |
| **Time to first review** | First review round for the 7 papers that were reviewed: 8.7, 11.4, 11.9, 12.3, 14.6, 17.7 and 28.9 weeks (mean about 15.1 weeks, shown on the journal page as 3.5 months) | n = 7; self-reported |
| **Time to acceptance (total)** | The 2 accepted papers in SciRev took 25.0 and 25.7 weeks in total (journal page shows 5.9 months); the 5 papers rejected after review took 8.7 to 28.9 weeks | n = 2 accepted |
| **Time to publication (after acceptance)** | 13 days average from acceptance to online publication, as printed in the publisher's journal-metrics block (https://www.tandfonline.com/journals/cshe20/about-this-journal, read 2026-11-23) | publisher page; averages, not distributions |

## Policies

### Peer Review

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Type** | Doubly anonymised refereeing by at least two referees after initial editor screening (aims text, archived journal home copy of 2025-11-18, http://web.archive.org/web/20251118174302/https://www.tandfonline.com/journals/cshe20). The archived instructions of 2022-12-20 carry the publisher's generic wording "single or double blind"; the later, journal-specific aims text is used here, but the live pages were not readable to confirm |
| **Transferable / Cascade?** | Blank. Not stated in the archived instructions |
| **Reviewer reports published?** | Blank. Not stated in the archived instructions |
| **Typical R+R rounds** | 1.4 review rounds on average as printed on the SciRev journal page (n = 10 reviews; https://scirev.org/journal/studies-in-higher-education/, retrieved 2026-11-23), with 2 or 3 review reports per reviewed paper (2 reports in 6 of the 7 reviewed papers, 3 reports in 1) |
| **Reviewer recommendations** | Blank. The archived instructions describe the editors selecting reviewers from their database and give no instruction on suggesting reviewers |
| **Desk-review stages** | Stage one: the editor in chief judges the abstract for contribution to theory or to policy and practice in higher education and for interest to an international audience; stage two: an associate editor checks theoretical foundations, methodology and conclusions before choosing reviewers. The same text says resubmitting the same manuscript after a desk rejection is not an option and that the abstract limit was raised from 150 to 250 words for this reason (archived instructions, 2022-12-20). The editor in chief and the senior editor describe the same desk-first approach in 2026 (https://www.timeshighereducation.com/node/745759) |

## Format

> Source: archived copy of the journal's instructions for authors dated 2022-12-20 (page footer "Updated 9th December 2022"), http://web.archive.org/web/20221220150104/https://www.tandfonline.com/action/authorSubmission?show=instructions&journalCode=cshe20; scope statements from the archived home copy of 2025-11-18. The live pages returned 403, so values may have changed.

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Article types accepted** | Empirical, theoretical and conceptual articles of significant originality, grounded in the higher education literature (aims text, home copy 2025-11-18). The aims list what is not published: studies not explicitly tied to the higher education literature; rapid or scoping reviews that synthesise prior research without novel arguments or theoretical insight; manuscripts on narrow questions in sub-specialties with little connection to broader debates; conceptual pieces without in-depth engagement with theoretical debates and without significantly novel arguments; policy reports and think pieces. The aims also say work on a more local or regional topic may fit a specialist journal better |
| **Word limit** | "A typical paper for this journal should be no more than 7000 words", inclusive of tables, references, figure or table captions and endnotes; authors are asked to include a word count (archived instructions, 2022-12-20) |
| **Word limit negotiability** | Blank. The instructions word the limit as a typical-paper ceiling; no statement on exceptions found |
| **Abstract limit** | Unstructured abstract of 250 words (raised from 150, per the instructions); 5 to 6 keywords; optional graphical abstract (landscape 2:1) and optional video abstract (archived instructions) |
| **Reference limit** | No separate cap found; references count inside the 7000 words. The reference style is linked ("this reference style") without being named in the page text, plus an EndNote style |
| **Supplementary material** | Supplemental material (video, dataset, fileset, sound file) is published online via Figshare (archived instructions) |
| **Figure/Table limits** | No count limit found. Tables should present new information rather than repeat the text and be supplied as editable files; figure resolution requirements are given; colour is free online and charged in print (GBP 300 per figure, 2022 copy) |
| **Style / submission format** | Any spelling style if consistent; Word or LaTeX (LaTeX as PDF plus source files), not PDF alone; Routledge Submission Portal; Crossref similarity screening during review and production; all authors give full name and affiliation on the cover page, affiliation being where the research was conducted; short biographical note per author (up to 200 words); the page lists a generic section order (introduction, materials and methods, results, discussion) as template text |

### Framing Requirements

- **Mandatory framing?** Yes, stated by the journal. Manuscripts are expected to be grounded in the higher education literature and to contribute to it through new empirical findings or novel insights (aims, archived home copy 2025-11-18, http://web.archive.org/web/20251118174302/https://www.tandfonline.com/journals/cshe20). The editors' first question is whether the article contributes to theoretical advancement or to improving policy and practice in higher education, and the second whether it will interest an international and diverse audience; the abstract is the main basis for that judgement (archived instructions 2022-12-20).
- **What kind of engagement?** Theory-or-practice contribution tied to higher education scholarship; the aims name policy, institutional management and performance, teaching and learning, and higher education's contribution to society and the economy; comparative and cross-national work is "particularly welcomed" (same aims text).
- **Article type and length**: up to about 7000 words including references, a 250-word abstract and 5-6 keywords (archived instructions).
- **Special-issue framing seen**: two special issues a year with a global theme; the issue of volume 50, issue 10 (2025) was on competition dynamics in higher education systems in East Asia (archived home copy 2025-11-18); a 50th Anniversary Issue of 17 articles is announced for November 2026 (https://srhe.ac.uk/publications/studies-in-higher-education/).
- **Consequences of ignoring it**: the aims list manuscript kinds the journal does not publish (see Format), say the rejection rate is higher than the editors would like, and tell authors with local or regional topics to consider specialist journals. SciRev reports include a desk rejection for being out of scope after 19 days and another, which the author calls subjective, after 13 days (https://scirev.org/reviews/studies-in-higher-education/); n = 2 reports of that kind, not a rate.

### Methodological Preferences

> Counts are articles of this source dated 2021-01-01 to 2026-11-23 whose title or abstract matches the regex (Python `re`, case-insensitive unless marked). Denominator: 923 articles with an abstract in OpenAlex of 936 articles in the window (98.6% coverage). Scoring convention of this research pass (its own, not an external standard): hits = 0 gives 0; share under 1% gives 1; 1-5% gives 2; over 5% gives 3; 4-5 only with a cited editorial statement, and none was judged to support it. Scores measure how often a method appears in abstracts, not how reviewers judge it. Retrieved 2026-11-23.

| Qualitative interviews | 3 | `interview(s\|ed\|ing)?` 239 (25.89%); `qualitative` 141 (15.28%); thematic analysis or grounded theory 50 (5.42%); `case stud(y\|ies)` 64 (6.93%) |

| Mixed methods | 3 | `mixed[- ]methods?` 48 (5.20%) |
| Meta-analysis / systematic review | 1 | `meta-analys[ie]s` 3 (0.33%); `systematic (literature )?review` 7 (0.76%); `scoping review` 6 (0.65%). The aims exclude rapid or scoping reviews that synthesise prior research without novel arguments (aims text) |

### Voice & Style

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **First-person voice acceptance (0-5)** | Not scored; no first-person rule found in the archived instructions. Sample: 375 of 923 abstract-bearing articles (40.6%) contain I, my, we or our in the abstract (regex `\b(I|my|we|our)\b`, case-sensitive; plural "we" may be generic). Of the 10 most recently dated abstract-bearing articles (2026-11-06 to 2026-11-16), 2 contain it: https://doi.org/10.1080/03075079.2026.2757168 and https://doi.org/10.1080/03075079.2026.2756475; the other 8 do not (for example https://doi.org/10.1080/03075079.2026.2755374, https://doi.org/10.1080/03075079.2026.2764326). OpenAlex works API, retrieved 2026-11-23 |
| **Expected density** | About 7000 words including references and captions; 250-word abstract (archived instructions, 2022-12-20). The editors say the abstract is the most important part of the submission because desk review rests on it (same copy) |
| **Writing style notes** | Any spelling style if consistent; reference style linked but not named in the page text; generic empirical section order listed as template text; short author biographies requested (archived instructions) |
| **Authorship pattern** | Crossref author lists for 970 of the 978 journal-article records of 2021-01 to 2026-11-23 (https://api.crossref.org/works?filter=issn:0307-5079,from-pub-date:2021-01-01,until-pub-date:2026-11-23): 1 author 155 (16.0%), 2 authors 279, 3 authors 236, 4 or more 300 |

### Reviewer Pool Characteristics

Reviewer behaviour itself is not observable from public pages; what follows is what public pages do show.

| Aspect | Detail | Evidence |
|--------|--------|----------|
| **Dominant tradition** | Current editorial team of 9 on the society page, with the chair of the Editorial Advisory Board named but the advisory members not listed; countries counted in Epistemological & Political Leanings. The editors say a first read by the editor in chief is followed by a read by one of the associate editors before reviewers are chosen from a database (archived instructions 2022-12-20; the senior editor, in 2026, describes abstracts read first by the editor in chief and then passed to "five assistant editors"; the society page lists five associate editors). Which disciplines reviewers come from is not published | https://srhe.ac.uk/publications/studies-in-higher-education/ ; https://www.timeshighereducation.com/node/745759 ; archived instructions above |
| **Review model** | Doubly anonymised, at least two referees, after editor screening (aims text, archived 2025-11-18); the 2022 instructions copy carries a generic "single or double blind" line | http://web.archive.org/web/20251118174302/https://www.tandfonline.com/journals/cshe20 |
| **Reviewer competence variance** | Mixed in first-hand reports, n = 10 reviews: report quality rated 3.0, 1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0, 2.0 and 2.0 out of 5 by the seven authors of reviewed papers (average printed on the journal page 2.4 of 5); one comment says some reviewers "suggested they failed to understand the message of the paper" and another that reviewers were "highly competent"; self-reported and self-selected | https://scirev.org/reviews/studies-in-higher-education/ ; https://scirev.org/journal/studies-in-higher-education/ |
| **Quantitative mindset bias on qualitative work?** | Blank. No reviewer-level source. Public counts show interview terms in 25.89% and survey or questionnaire terms in 19.07% of abstract-bearing articles (regexes in Methodological Preferences), which says nothing about how reviewers treat either | OpenAlex counts, see Methodological Preferences |
| **Discourse community signals (editorial board)** | Author side: GB 230, US 101, AU 100, CN 99, DE 61 of 936 articles have at least one author in the country (OpenAlex). Editor side: 9 current entries in Canada, Italy, UK, Ireland, Malaysia and the Netherlands | OpenAlex works API (retrieved 2026-11-23); society page above |

### Practical Concerns

| Concern | Detail |
|---------|--------|
| **IRB requirement strictness** | No ethics-approval rule found on the archived instructions: the "Peer Review and Ethics" section only points to the publisher's general publishing-ethics guidance (archived 2022-12-20). The publisher's current ethics rules and the live instructions were not read |
| **Single-author acceptance** | Single-author papers are a minority but common: 155 of 970 Crossref records with author lists (16.0%) in 2021-01 to 2026-11-23; 3-author and 4+-author papers together are 536 (55.3%) |
| **Independent scholar friendliness** | Blank. The archived instructions define author affiliation as where the research was conducted and state no rule for authors without an institution; no count of independent-scholar authors was made |
| **Data transparency requirement** | None found: the archived instructions contain no data-availability or data-sharing section (page text searched for "data availability", "data sharing" and "data policy": no match); supplemental material goes to Figshare |
| **OPSEC compatibility** | Doubly anonymised per the aims text, but the archived instructions ask all authors to put full name and affiliation on the cover page, and warn that anonymity cannot be guaranteed once a manuscript is on a preprint server (archived 2022-12-20). Pre-submission preprints are allowed by the publisher (https://authorservices.taylorandfrancis.com/research-impact/sharing-versions-of-journal-articles/, read live 2026-11-23). How the live submission portal handles anonymisation was not read |
| **AI use** | Disclosure statement required at publisher level; AI cannot be an author (https://taylorandfrancis.com/our-policies/ai-policy/, read live 2026-11-23). Journal-specific wording unknown |
| **Open access and cost** | Hybrid (Open Select); no submission, publication or page charges for the non-OA route per the 2022 copy; OA APC not readable; SRHE members have reduced APCs per the 2022 copy; 423 of 936 recent articles are hybrid open access in OpenAlex |
| **Resubmission after desk rejection** | The archived instructions say resubmitting the same manuscript after desk rejection is not an option |

### AI-Research Notes (sources, blanks, and cross-language checks)

**signal_quality (0-5)**: overall 3. Per layer: OpenAlex counts (methods, topics, countries, types) 4 (98.6% abstract coverage over 936 articles); Crossref (year counts, issue numbers, author lists) 3; society page and special-issue PDF 4 (read live); journal-specific policies and guidelines 2 (live pages unreadable; archived copies of 2022-12-20, 2025-11-18 and 2022-06-20); publisher-wide policies 3; experiential layer 3 (SciRev n = 10; one trade-press article with the editors' own statements).

**Pages and what they supplied**: society page (frequency, founding, current editorial team, anniversary issue, chair of advisory board); archived journal home copy 2025-11-18 (aims, exclusions, peer-review wording, Open Select flag, special-issue and call items; HTML comments removed before reading, none held policy text); archived instructions copy 2022-12-20 (desk-review procedure, word and abstract limits, ethics and anonymity wording, APC discounts, fees); archived board copy 2022-06-20; special-issue guidelines PDF (live); Times Higher Education article on the 50th anniversary (editors' statements; its text gives about 4,500 submissions in the last year, which differs from a search-engine summary that said 7,500; the article text is used); T&F AI policy and sharing pages (live); SciRev journal and review pages.

**Experiential checks**: SciRev (https://scirev.org/journal/studies-in-higher-education/ and https://scirev.org/reviews/studies-in-higher-education/): 10 reviews, figures and per-review details recorded in Review Cycle Time and Reviewer Pool Characteristics. LetPub: the public search URL returned only its landing page, so no journal row. 小木虫 / 知乎: one web search for the journal name with 投稿 经验 审稿周期 拒稿 returned no muchong or zhihu thread; it surfaced one single-user desk-rejection report on a Chinese journal-info site (a desk reject three days after an October 2025 submission), which was not opened and is not recorded as evidence; fabiaoji not reached. Reddit: one web search for the journal with submission experience, desk reject, review time and reddit returned no Reddit thread.

**Needs real-browser read:** the current editorial board and advisory board and live aims on the about page were not re-read for this entry's earlier sections (https://www.tandfonline.com/journals/cshe20/about-this-journal itself read 2026-11-23 for the metrics block only); https://www.tandfonline.com/action/authorSubmission?show=instructions&journalCode=cshe20 (live instructions: AI item, ethics and data rules, current word limit); https://www.tandfonline.com/toc/cshe20/current; https://authorservices.taylorandfrancis.com/choose-open/publishing-open-access/open-access-cost-finder/ (APC and embargo). The authorSubmission and current-issue pages returned 403 to curl with a browser User-Agent and cookie jar, 5 tries each.

**Unreadable pages**: the T&F home, instructions and current-issue pages above, covered by the archived copies named in each section. The about page was readable on 2026-11-23 only after a cookie-priming request to the T&F home page.

**Fields deliberately left blank, and why**: i10-index and top topics (rate-limited or unread), transfer policy, reviewer-report publication, reviewer recommendations, word-limit negotiability, read-and-publish list, under-review preprint rule, independent-scholar rule, reviewer quantitative-bias row. Impact factor and quartile: paywalled, not stated by policy.

**Method note**: keyword counts come from a paged OpenAlex works pull (978 records, 5 requests at about 2-second spacing, no key, no 429), reconstructing abstracts from the inverted index and applying the regexes listed above locally. The next OpenAlex request, the scaffold call of `scripts/import_openalex.py`, returned HTTP 429, after which OpenAlex was not used again. Crossref supplied year counts, issue numbers and author lists.

## Strategic Notes

> Each statement below follows from a fact recorded above and names it. Where the evidence does not support a statement, the field says so.

### Hard Blockers

- **Scope**: the aims say the journal does not publish studies not explicitly connected to the higher education literature, narrow sub-specialty questions without broader connection, policy reports and think pieces, and scoping or rapid reviews without novel arguments (Format; aims text, archived 2025-11-18).
- **Conceptual work**: conceptual pieces without in-depth theoretical engagement and significantly novel arguments are excluded (Format; aims text).
- **Length and abstract**: about 7000 words including references and a 250-word abstract per the archived instructions; the live page could not be read, so these may have changed (Format).
- **Resubmission**: the same manuscript cannot be resubmitted after a desk rejection (Peer Review; archived instructions).
- **AI use**: undisclosed generative AI use breaches the publisher policy (AI Policy).

### Soft Tax

- **Desk review on the abstract**: the editors say the abstract decides the stage-one outcome and that high submission volume (about 4,500 in the last year per the senior editor) drives desk rejection (Peer Review, Metrics; archived instructions; https://www.timeshighereducation.com/node/745759).
- **Time**: in SciRev (n = 10), reviewed papers took 8.7 to 28.9 weeks for the first round, accepted papers 25.0 and 25.7 weeks in total, and one desk rejection took 168 days (Review Cycle Time); the publisher page prints averages of 8 days to first decision, 70 days to first post-review decision and 13 days from acceptance to online publication.
- **Open access cost**: the OA APC amount was not readable; a 2022 copy lists reduced APCs for SRHE members (Open Access).
- **Anonymisation and preprints**: preprint posting removes any anonymity guarantee per the archived instructions, while the aims describe doubly anonymised review (Practical Concerns).

### Best Suited For

- Empirical or theoretical studies of higher education with explicit ties to the higher education literature: students appear in 58.94% and academics or faculty in 50.49% of 923 abstracts; policy in 20.26% (Subject Density, Framing Requirements).
- Comparative, cross-national and international-theme work, which the aims call particularly welcome and which appears in 11.27% of abstracts (Framing Requirements, Epistemological & Political Leanings).
- Interview-based and survey-based studies: interview terms in 25.89% and survey or questionnaire terms in 19.07% of abstracts (Methodological Preferences).
- Work on AI in higher education: four of the five most-cited articles of 2021-2026 are on AI (Epistemological & Political Leanings); the editors also describe a desk policy against low-value AI-generated submissions, so such papers face a screen (Sensitive Topics).

### Not Recommended For

- Scoping reviews, rapid reviews and policy reports: stated exclusions in the aims, and review terms appear in 1.73% of abstracts (Format, Methodological Preferences).
- Narrowly local topics with no wider framing: the aims point such work to specialist journals (Format).
- Experimental or randomized designs as the main method: 13 of 923 abstracts (1.41%); this shows rarity, not rejection (Methodological Preferences).
- Anyone needing a verified decision-time or acceptance figure from the publisher: none was readable; only SciRev self-reports (n = 10) exist (Review Cycle Time, Metrics).

### Rejection Fallback Chain

> No source states where rejected authors usually go. The rows below are topical neighbours that already exist in this corpus, listed only because they share the subject area (higher education or education research); they are not a claim about acceptance odds or fit.

| Rank | Journal | Why this fallback works |
|------|---------|------------------------|
| 1 | [Teaching in Higher Education](teaching-in-higher-education.md) | Same subject area (higher education teaching and learning); an entry exists in this corpus. No fit evidence collected here |
| 2 | [British Educational Research Journal](british-educational-research-journal.md) | Same broad subject area (education research); an entry exists in this corpus. No fit evidence collected here |
| 3 | [International Journal of Educational Technology in Higher Education](international-journal-of-educational-technology-in-higher-education.md) | Higher education plus technology overlap (AI terms in 36 of 923 abstracts here); an entry exists in this corpus. No fit evidence collected here |
